claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me: **What is the name and age of the child (or children) you're asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'd like to know if I'm eligible for Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who is 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me gather a bit more detail about Alex's situation to assess your eligibility.

**Does Alex currently live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know.

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in school or college anymore.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

**Is Alex currently in paid work or self-employment?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex has started an apprenticeship recently - they're training in a trade.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's relevant to the eligibility rules.

Before I can give you a final answer, I need to check the specific eligibility criteria. Let me review the official Child Benefit rules.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I can see the key eligibility rules now. Based on the information provided, I can see that there's a specific rule about apprenticeships.

**To clarify - is Alex's apprenticeship in England, or is it in Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland?**

This is important because the rules differ depending on where the apprenticeship is taking place.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's in England. We live in England.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Based on the information you've provided, I now have all the details I need to make a determination.

According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you will **not be eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why: The rules state that you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child "starts an apprenticeship in England." Since Alex has started an apprenticeship in England, they no longer qualify under the Child Benefit scheme, even though they are under 20 and in training.

This is a specific rule that applies to apprenticeships in England - they don't count as "approved education or training" for Child Benefit purposes.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'm sorry that you're not eligible for Child Benefit in this case. If you have any other questions about your circumstances or would like to know more about other benefits you might be entitled to, feel free to contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office directly for further advice.
